title: Active Subscribers by Subscription Plan
description_markdown: Subscription ops request: For each subscription plan (`plan_name`), count total active subscribers as `subscriber_count`, and calculate monthly recurring revenue (`SUM(monthly_price)` as `mrr`). Filter for `status = 'active'`. Return `plan_name`, `subscriber_count`, and `mrr`. Order by `mrr` DESC.
starter_query:
-- Plan subscriber counts
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT plan_name, COUNT(*) AS subscriber_count, SUM(monthly_price) AS mrr FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'active' GROUP BY plan_name ORDER BY mrr DESC, plan_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Groups active subscription tiers to compute recurring cash flow.

title: Identify Most Watched Movies with Full Completion
description_markdown: Content licensing request: Count how many times each movie was watched with 100% completion (`completed_percentage = 100`) as `completion_count`. Return `m.title`, `m.genre`, and `completion_count`. Filter for `completion_count >= 1`. Order by `completion_count` DESC, `m.title` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Most completed movies
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT m.title, m.genre, COUNT(w.watch_id) AS completion_count FROM movies m JOIN watch_history w ON m.movie_id = w.movie_id WHERE w.completed_percentage = 100 GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.genre HAVING COUNT(w.watch_id) >= 1 ORDER BY completion_count DESC, m.title ASC;
solution_explanation: Measures engagement retention on digital titles.
hints: Filter `completed_percentage = 100`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT m.title, m.genre, COUNT(w.watch_id) AS completion_count FROM movies m JOIN watch_history w ON m.movie_id = w.movie_id WHERE w.completed_percentage = 100 GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.genre HAVING COUNT(w.watch_id) >= 1 ORDER BY completion_count DESC, m.title ASC;

title: Flag Cancelled Accounts with Viewing History
description_markdown: Retention marketing request: Find users who cancelled their subscription (`subscriptions.status = 'cancelled'`) but have logged at least one watch history entry. solution_explanation: Joins user subscription status to watch metrics to support win-back campaigns.
hints: Join users -> subscriptions -> watch_history.

Query: WITH user_views AS (SELECT u.user_id, u.username, COUNT(w.watch_id) AS watch_count FROM streaming_users u JOIN watch_history w ON u.user_id = w.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.username) SELECT username, watch_count FROM user_views WHERE watch_count > (SELECT AVG(watch_count) FROM user_views) ORDER BY watch_count DESC, username ASC;

title: Track Chronological Viewing Intervals Using LEAD
description_markdown: For each watch event, fetch the timestamp of the user's next consecutive streaming session as `next_watched_at` using `LEAD()`. Return `watch_id`, `user_id`, `watched_at`, and `next_watched_at`. Order by `user_id` ASC, `watched_at` ASC, `watch_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT watch_id, user_id, watched_at, LEAD(watched_at, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watched_at ASC, watch_id ASC) AS next_watched_at FROM watch_history ORDER BY user_id ASC, watched_at ASC, watch_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses LEAD(watched_at, 1) partitioned by user_id ordered chronologically.
hints: Use `LEAD(watched_at, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watched_at ASC, watch_id ASC)`.
Order by `user_id` ASC, `watched_at` ASC, `watch_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT watch_id, user_id, watched_at, LEAD(watched_at, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watched_at ASC, watch_id ASC) AS next_watched_at FROM watch_history ORDER BY user_id ASC, watched_at ASC, watch_id ASC;

title: Compile Subscriber Engagement and Consumption Profile
description_markdown: Compile a full subscriber analytics profile showing `username`, `country`, `plan_name`, `status`, total viewing events (`total_watches`), and average completion percentage (`avg_completion`, default 0.0). Order by `total_watches` DESC, `avg_completion` DESC, `username` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT u.username, u.country, s.plan_name, s.status, COUNT(w.watch_id) AS total_watches, COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(w.completed_percentage), 1), 0.0) AS avg_completion FROM streaming_users u JOIN subscriptions s ON u.user_id = s.user_id LEFT JOIN watch_history w ON u.user_id = w.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.username, u.country, s.plan_name, s.status ORDER BY total_watches DESC, avg_completion DESC, u.username ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins users and subscriptions, LEFT JOINs watch_history, and aggregates session counts and completion rates.
hints: Join `streaming_users` and `subscriptions`, LEFT JOIN `watch_history`.
Use `COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(w.completed_percentage), 1), 0.0) AS avg_completion`.

Query: SELECT u.username, u.country, s.plan_name, s.status, COUNT(w.watch_id) AS total_watches, COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(w.completed_percentage), 1), 0.0) AS avg_completion FROM streaming_users u JOIN subscriptions s ON u.user_id = s.user_id LEFT JOIN watch_history w ON u.user_id = w.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.username, u.country, s.plan_name, s.status ORDER BY total_watches DESC, avg_completion DESC, u.username ASC;
